import ssl

class WebSocketClient:
    def __init__(self, uri):
        self.uri = uri

    async def connect(self):
        context = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT)
        context.check_hostname = True
        context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE

        reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection(self.uri, ssl=context)

        message = 'Hello, world'
        writer.write(message.encode())
        await writer.drain()

        data = await reader.read()
        print(f'Received: {data.decode()}')

        await writer.drain()
        writer.close()
        await writer.wait_closed()

But Newton had a tendency to be argumentative and combative - he famously feuded with Robert Hooke and Gottfried Leibniz over the discovery of calculus.

Euler was likely the most prolific mathematician of all time, publishing over 800 books and papers. He made key discoveries in fields as varied as topology, number theory, and graph theory. Euler also blinded one eye while working with an air pump and later lost sight in his other eye.

Gauss was a child prodigy known as the "Prince of Mathematics". He made groundbreaking discoveries in algebra, number theory, statistics, and many other domains. Gauss had very few close friendships and was known to keep to himself most of the time.

I think it would be fascinating to get these mathematical giants together and have a conversation about their discoveries and views on the nature of mathematics. But with only Gauss likely being very quiet and the others having complicated personal histories, I'm not sure what the atmosphere would be like!
